museum.blurb: Not a Commodore 128, despite what the screen says. This is the CBM-II — Commodore's 1982 attempt to sell a serious business computer, built on a 6509 that reaches a full megabyte by bank-switching, and cancelled almost immediately.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 12 kiosk runs VICE (xcbm2 -model 610) emulating a PAL CBM 610; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. VICE bundles the CBM-II ROMs, so this tile needs no external media — the 610 boots to BASIC with nothing attached. NOT A NEAR-DUPLICATE OF cbm8032, and the placard says why: same green 80-column CBM banner, but a 6509 bank-switching a megabyte instead of a 6502 with 32 KB, a low-profile box with a detached monitor instead of an all-in-one, and a business market Commodore reached for and missed. The golden is the machine's own untouched power-on screen; the visitor types at the BASIC prompt through the SPA on-screen keyboard. Keyboard-only exhibit; native 704x528 window on an 800x600 X root (the doubled window is silently clipped by every root this fleet uses). See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/cbm2.md. The screen reads "commodore basic 128": that name predates the Commodore 128 of 1985 and shares nothing with it.

reset.fixture: Commodore CBM 610 (PAL) power-on screen — "*** commodore basic 128, v4.0 ***" and "ready." in green on black at 80 columns — in VICE xcbm2 -model 610, native size on an 800x600 X root; golden INTERNAL snapshot restores the untouched cold boot. Nothing is curated and nothing is typed before the bake, and no keys are sent after the restore. Keyboard certified 2026-08-09 AFTER the bake against the restored fixture: PRINT 3 at the tile's own 80/80 pacing extended the lit text from rows 100..162 to rows 100..226 (BASIC echoed the line, printed " 3" and painted a second "ready."), then loadvm golden returned the frame to the baked bounding box exactly. A pixel-count test was rejected as unfalsifiable here — the blinking cursor gives back what the new lines add (456 -> 454). Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); AC97 audio.
